discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn

motivation: Ground-based interferometers opened the audio band of gravitational waves. Pulsar timing arrays have now opened the nanohertz band, a window roughly ten orders of magnitude lower in frequency. In 2023, NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA and CPTA published coordinated evidence for a stochastic background showing the Hellings–Downs angular correlation, the signature of spacetime itself fluctuating across the Galaxy. The most likely source is the cosmic population of supermassive black-hole binaries. McLaughlin co-founded NANOGrav and led the decades of precision millisecond-pulsar timing it required. Siemens developed the detection statistics and noise modelling that made the claimed significance credible, and led NANOGrav through the evidence era. Kramer built European and international timing programmes and set the standards for pulsar-based tests of gravity. Together they turned a galaxy of pulsars into a gravitational-wave observatory. That is a new observational window, and it was made robust through careful work on significance.
